_guide: Example intake for a web app. Scopes were chosen AFTER running the stack generator, to match the tree it produced (SCAFFOLD.md step 4).
name: Field Service Scheduler
summary: A web app where a dispatcher assigns service jobs to technicians and technicians see their day on a phone.

scopes.title: Routes and pages
scopes.covers: Next.js App Router pages, layouts and route handlers (the HTTP API under src/app/api).
rules: Route handlers stay thin: parse, call src/lib, respond.
Every route handler has a test under src/app/**/__tests__.

scopes.title: UI components
scopes.covers: Reusable React components and their stories.
rules: Components are presentational; they receive data as props.

scopes.title: Domain and data
scopes.covers: Scheduling rules, data access, auth helpers. Server-only.
rules: Unit-test every scheduling rule with vitest.

brief.problem: Dispatchers plan the day on a whiteboard and call each technician, so changes are lost and customers wait.
goals: A dispatcher can assign a job to a technician and see conflicts
A technician sees today's jobs in order
success: An end-to-end test assigns a job and the technician view shows it
Assigning two overlapping jobs to one technician shows a conflict

constraints: Technicians see only their own jobs; checked on the server.
